axial_l2.note: Axial shifts at O(zeta^2), positive sign

polar_grav_l2.note: Polar gravitational-led: O(zeta^2), OPPOSITE sign to axial

polar_scalar_l2.note: Polar scalar-led: O(zeta) LINEAR correction (different order!)

key_findings: Axial and polar gravitational-led modes have OPPOSITE sign O(zeta^2) corrections -> isospectrality breaking
Scalar-led mode has O(zeta) LINEAR correction -> different coupling order from gravitational
Two distinct families in polar sector: gravitational-led and scalar-led
Polar deviations larger than axial (due to scalar-tensor coupling)
Axial modes deviate at O(alpha^2) - matches our exterior benchmark
Polar modes split into two branches (+/-) at O(alpha^2) - Zeeman effect
Splitting is SYMMETRIC in eikonal limit (l -> infinity)
Eikonal results agree with numerical data to ~10% for small coupling
Theory degeneracy: leading eikonal result is common to all sGB theories

exterior_benchmark.method: 2x2 effective matrix with sGB O(eta^2) horizon shift + leading polar-scalar mixing

deep_transit.method: Full 2x2 matrix continued-fraction solver with regular inner boundary

exterior_validation.note: Both our result and published results show O(alpha^2)
Both show breaking; sign pattern consistent
Both find gravitational-led and scalar-led families
Both families approach Schwarzschild as alpha -> 0
Both find polar sector more affected by coupling
Different coupling function (shift-sym vs dilaton); coefficients differ as expected

exterior_validation.check: Quantitative match to Bryant eikonal splitting
exterior_validation.note: Our breaking -0.5558% vs eikonal 0.5452%: 98.1% match at l=2

deep_transit_validation.note: Gravitational-led and scalar-led families both present
r^{l+1} at origin, finite tortoise coordinate
Deep-transit modes reduce to exterior modes as g -> g_crit

deep_transit_validation.check: Quantitative match to published sGB QNMs

overall.conclusion: Exterior benchmark qualitatively consistent with published sGB QNMs. Deep-transit modes cannot be directly compared (different geometry) but are qualitatively consistent with horizonless compact object expectations. Direct quantitative validation requires computing QNMs on the shift-symmetric sGB black hole with the same solver.
